div.head: Forf 3.1
div.ab: . . . æt ælcon ðeofstolenan orfe ⁊ be his . . . forfange sylle, þæt is æt ælcon scill' penig, sy ðæs cynnes orf ðe hit sy, gyf hit man æt ðeofes handa ahret.

Sed antiquum rectum est, ut de omni furtiuo pecore secundum precium estimatum forfang reddatur, id est de uno quoque sol. unus denarius, sit eiusmodi pecus quod sit, si a (de) latronum manibus excuciatur.
Uetus rectum quidem est, ut pro omni furata pecunia secundum precium ipsius anticipacio detur, id est pro solido nummus, cuiuscunque generis pecunia sit, si a manibus furis erepta sit;

Aber echtes Recht ist, dass fehlt B) Einfang von jedem gestohlenen Vieh gemäss dessen (Werth fehlt B) gezahlt werde, nämlich von jedem Schilling [1] Pfennig, sei es Vieh von welcher Art es auch sei, wenn es [nämlich] aus Diebes Hand entrissen wird.

But true law is that — lacking in B) seizure-money be paid for every stolen beast according to its (value — lacking in B), namely [1] penny for every shilling, of whatever kind the beast may be, if [that is] it is snatched from the thief's hand.
.. for all stolen property and by its … [reward for] recovery was at [the ratio of] one penny per shilling, whatever kind of property it was, as long as it was recovered from thieves.
div.note: U: translator unrecorded: check; In B, ‘⁊’ should be struck, and there is no gap after ‘his’: read ‘weorþe forfang’. K: ‘ut se omni fortiuo’ corrected to ‘ut de omni furtiuo’ against Liebermann.; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 391, October 2026 (MS Cons)
